request.spec:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias (as names are
compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge
does (claims after theirs, aliases joined, bound figures lost); the other sheet writes
PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> from=<sheet id> then PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias (as names are
compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge
does (claims after theirs, aliases joined, bound figures lost); the other sheet writes

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A transfer to a sheet that already has someone with the same name or alias now merges the arriving person into that person instead of being refused. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests. My last edit after that run only changed a doc comment.

**What happens now** (`person/TransferPerson.java`):
- **Normal transfer first:** the person is moved as before. Their claims are renumbered on the other sheet, and the figures their statements had fixed are dropped.
- **Then the merge:** if anyone on the other sheet shares their name or one of their aliases (ignoring case and surrounding spaces), the arrival is merged into that person using the existing merge code. Their claims are listed after the existing person's, their name and aliases become that person's aliases, and the rest of them (including their contact) is dropped.
- **Audit lines:** the other sheet records `PERSON_TRANSFERRED … from=<sheet id>` and then `PERSON_MERGED … from=<name> into=<name>`, followed by the usual ROLLUP and TOTALS lines.

**Database change:** aliases were unique per sheet, but the test expects Ada to end up with both "Addie" and "addie". I added `V62__person_alias_merged.sql`, which turns that unique index into a plain one. The screens still refuse a duplicate alias when someone adds one by hand. Aliases are now also sorted with a fixed tie-break, so "Addie" always lists before "addie".

**Cases the request didn't cover — my choices:**
- **Matches more than one person** (say the name matches one and an alias matches another): refused.
- **The match is retired:** refused, the same as a merge.
- **Contact clash:** this is only checked when there's no merge, because a merged person's contact is dropped anyway.

I also updated the refusal message on the screen and the comments on the transfer endpoint and `api.ts` to match.
